IncidentEvents.message:
The feature disruption affecting Apex code compilation and deployment is resolved. We rolled affected instances back to the previous version, and all instances are now running on it. Customers can compile and deploy Apex code again.

We apologize for how this incident affected you and your business. We will undertake a full investigation of the incident, establishing the underlying cause, and preventive action to avoid a repeat in the future.

We've nearly finished rolling back the affected instances to the previous version. A few instances needed a second attempt, and we've now completed those. We're closely monitoring the small number of instances that are still finishing. Customers on those instances may still see intermittent failures when compiling or deploying Apex code.

We’ll provide another update in 60 minutes or sooner if additional information becomes available.

We continue to address a feature disruption affecting a subset of customers on instances that received a recent software release. 

Several rollbacks have completed, and recovery has been confirmed on a prioritized affected instance. Validation is underway on additional instances while the broader rollback continues. Until the rollback completes, some customers may continue to experience intermittent failures, when compiling or deploying Apex code. Depending on how the affected code is used, login flows and related business processes may also fail.

We’ll provide another update in 60 minutes or sooner if additional information becomes available.

We have started rolling affected instances back to the previous version, prioritizing the environments with confirmed customer impact. The broader rollback is now in progress, and teams will validate recovery as each instance completes.

We're also preparing a corrective release that removes the triggering runtime-library change before the affected release is deployed again.

We’ll provide another update in 30 minutes or sooner if additional information becomes available.

We are investigating a feature disruption affecting some customers on instances that received a recent release. Affected customers may experience failures when compiling or deploying Apex code. In some cases, customers may also be unable to log in or complete processes that depend on the affected Apex code. The behavior is intermittent and depends on the specific code being compiled.

We've identified an update to a supporting runtime library in the recent release as the likely trigger. Further deployment of the release has been halted, and teams are working to return affected instances to the previous version. A corrective release is also being prepared as a fallback.

We’ll provide another update in 30 minutes or sooner if additional information becomes available.
During investigations, we established that the level of impact differs from what was initially understood. We have updated the incident posting to reflect the current impact symptoms accurately.

IncidentEvents.message:
The issue affecting custom actions in the Field Service Lightning (FSL) Dispatch and Scheduling Console in sandbox environments is now resolved. At 16:23 UTC, we completed the rollback of the release on all impacted sandbox instances. Customers can once again view and use their custom actions and resume any blocked sandbox deployments. Production environments weren't affected. 

We apologize for how this incident affected you and your business. We will undertake a full investigation of the incident, establishing the technical trigger, the underlying cause, and preventive action to avoid a repeat in the future.

The rollback is complete on almost all impacted sandbox instances. Customers on those instances should now be able to view and use their custom actions in the FSL (Field Service Lightning) Dispatch and Scheduling Console. One remaining instance is taking longer than expected, and our teams are actively working to complete its rollback. Production environments aren't affected. 

We'll provide an update in 60 minutes or sooner if additional information becomes available.

We're still rolling back the release across all sandbox instances that received it, and we're monitoring its progress closely.

We'll provide an update in 60 minutes or sooner if additional information becomes available.

The rollback is taking longer than anticipated. This is due to a subset of instances requiring a manual rollback by our team. Despite this delay, the overall rollback is progressing well. 

We'll provide an update in 60 minutes or sooner if additional information becomes available.

We're continuing to roll back the release on sandbox instances. We're monitoring its progress and have additional resources on standby in case the rollback doesn't succeed.

We'll provide an update in 60 minutes or sooner if additional information becomes available.

We’ve completed the testing of the rollback and have validated that it was succesful. We’re working to perform a rollback on all impacted instances which received the release. This is expected to several hours to complete. We will continue to monitor it’s progress. 

We'll provide an update in 60 minutes or sooner if additional information becomes available.

We're aware of an issue affecting the Field Service Lightning (FSL) Dispatch and Scheduling Console in sandbox environments. Customers can’t view or use their custom actions, which may block some sandbox deployments. Production environments aren’t affected. We’ve identified a recent release change as the likely trigger of the issue. We've paused further rollout of the release. We’re testing a rollback of the release to see if this brings customers out of impact. 

We'll provide an update in 30 minutes or sooner if additional information becomes available.
